title: KPI derivation lifecycle and rollout signal notebook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working tracker and signal notebook for deriving launch KPIs from product roadmap milestones and mapping them to operational readiness signals. Use this as the canonical place to capture origin metrics, assumptions, transformation logic, and paired fallbacks for each launch metric.

Executive summary (tl;dr):
- We need a compact mapping from product feature outputs -> user-visible telemetry -> SLO/KPI definitions -> alert/rollback triggers.
- Goal: reduce ambiguity so SRE, Support, and Product can run a deterministic fast-go/no-go check for phased rollouts.
- This doc contains: derivation examples, cadence checklist, a compact tracker table (described below), risk/assumption log, and an owner roster for the first 30d post-launch.

How to use this doc (quick):
1) For each feature in the upcoming sprint, add a row to the tracker table with: feature name, primary user journey, signal(s), derivation note, baseline, expected delta, target KPI, alert thresholds, fallback action, owners.
2) Link any dashboards / synthetic probes in "linked_artifacts" — dashboards must map to the exact signal name used here.
3) During the launch-readiness sync we will iterate the targets and lock the final thresholds 48 hours before canary traffic starts.

Tracker table (textual representation for this sheet):
- Columns (explainers):
  - id: short numeric id for cross-ref (e.g., 001)
  - feature: short feature name
  - journey: which user flow is affected (onboarding, generate, embed, billing)
  - signal_name: exact metric name to be emitted by instrumentation team (snake_case)
  - raw_metric: event / gauge / histogram name + units (e.g., request_latency_ms p50/p95, tokens_per_request)
  - derivation_note: how KPI is computed from raw_metric (simple formula or transforms)
  - baseline: current measured baseline (where available) and time window (e.g., p95 420ms last 14d)
  - expected_delta: directional expectation (+10% latency, -3% success)
  - target_kpi: launch target (e.g., p95 latency <= 600ms, error_rate <= 0.5%)
  - alert_threshold: immediate paging threshold and advisory threshold
  - fallback_action: what happens if threshold crossed (e.g., degrade to smaller model, route to backup region, rollback feature flag)
  - primary_owner: name and pager contact
 - Example row (freeform):
   - id: 001
   - feature: streaming-response-v2
   - journey: chat_v1
   - signal_name: streaming_token_flush_rate
   - raw_metric: flush_ms (gauge), p95
   - derivation_note: KPI = p95(flush_ms) aggregated by route, compare to baseline 14d
   - baseline: p95 22ms (14d)
   - expected_delta: +8ms under heavy traffic
   - target_kpi: p95 <= 45ms during canary
   - alert_threshold: page if p95 > 90ms for 5m, advisory if p95 > 45ms for 10m
   - fallback_action: throttle to 50rps per instance, disable streaming, route to polling
   - primary_owner: Diego Alvarez (pager: pager:D-Alvarez)

KPI derivation examples (concise):
- Throughput economics (cost per 1k tokens): combine token_count emitted / infra_cpu_seconds + GPU-cost-per-second; normalize to USD/1k tokens. Use last 7d for smoothing; raise advisory if cost/1k increases > 12% vs baseline.
- Per-route success_rate: success_rate = 1 - (count(error_codes >=500) / total_requests) aggregated per route. Use p99 windows.
- Latency SLAs: compute p95 over user-visible surface; ignore synthetic traffic and known-bot user-agents.

Rollout cadence and gating checklist (cookbook style):
- T-7d: Finalize tracker rows for every route affected. Confirm instrumentation exists for each signal_name. QA: sampling tests + dashboard stub.
- T-3d: Define canary cohort size and ramp schedule. Lock target_kpi and alert_thresholds. Owners confirmed.
- T-1d: Smoke synthetic against canary; run the smoke playbook (see linked_playbook).
- Day0 (canary start): Start at 1% traffic, watch advisory signals for 30m, then 5% for 2h, then 20% for 6h if stable.
- Decision points: if any page threshold fires, immediate pause and execute rollback or fallback as defined in row; if only advisory thresholds, call ops triage and consider slow ramp.

Risk & assumptions ledger (short list):
- Assumption A: dashboard raw metrics are being emitted with the same cardinality as prod (if not, targets may be invalid).
- Assumption B: background batch jobs that affect token usage are offline during canary (if not, cost metrics will be noisy).
- Known risk: shared caching layer TTL change could introduce spikiness in p95 latency. Contingency = pin TTL to previous value for first 48h.

Owner roster (first 30d watch):
- Weekdays 9–18 primary: Product-ops (Sofia Chen) / Product (Marcus) / SRE lead (Diego)
- Night/weekend escalation: On-call SRE (rota) -> On-call Product-Eng backup.
- Customer success contact for canary customers: Aisha Thompson (need to prepare proactive comms).

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- TODO: ask infra to add streaming_token_flush_rate to aggregation pipeline (ticket JIRA-OBS-1293).
- Question: do we treat short-lived error spikes from A/B test harnesses as signal? proposal: annotate test traffic and exclude.
- TODO: build a small synthetic that exercises the model bundle variants to produce baseline for quantization mode. Owner: Marcus.

Post-launch measurement plan (30/60/90 slices):
- 0–30d: daily telemetry + incident tempo log. Weekly retrospective on KPI drift.
- 31–60d: move to weekly measurement; collect regression candidate prompt sets and run quality evals.
- 61–90d: finalize cost/performance tuning recommendations and feed into Redwood Optimize backlog.

Compact checklist for the launch-readiness sync (copy into the meeting agenda):
- [ ] All tracker rows created and validated
- [ ] Dashboards linked and smoke-tested
- [ ] Canary ramp plan locked
- [ ] Owners and pager details documented
- [ ] Communication plan to CS and pilot customers
- [ ] Rollback/fallback validated with dry-run

Notes on format & hygiene (drive doc conventions):
- Keep metric names snake_case and stable; if a name changes, add a new row instead of mutating the old one (preserve history).
- When threshold values are changed, add a single-line change log with date and author in the table cell.
- Use the linked_artifacts field at the top to capture authoritative dashboard URLs and runbook fragments.

Appendix: short glossary
- advisory threshold: early warning, ops notification but not automatic downgrade/paging
- page threshold: triggers on-call paging and immediate stop of ramp
- baseline: median or p95 measured over the last N days (N must be explicit in the derivation_note)

End of doc.

Patch notes: initial creation 2024-11-12 by Sofia Chen. Iteration 2025-02-03 added cost-per-1k token derivation and owner roster.
